summaries: A defector and two of his staff are hiding near a disused desert strip. They carry design data for a new anti-ship missile. Put down on the strip, take them aboard and get out before the patrols return.
Allied special forces have cleared a dirt runway deep inside hostile territory. A crate of captured guidance electronics is waiting there. Land, load it into the bay and leave without lingering.
A reconnaissance team has been cut off far from the coast. Their exfiltration helicopter was lost. The only way out is a short dirt strip they have marked for you. Land and bring them home.
Technicians have dismantled a seeker head from a downed enemy missile and need it flown out tonight. The pickup is a graded strip in the desert, unlit and unguarded. Do not stay on the ground long.
A courier with codebooks from an enemy signals unit is waiting at a remote landing ground. Touch down, take the package and be airborne again within minutes.
An informant inside the enemy air staff wants out. He will be at an abandoned strip with his family. Land there, pick them up and fly them to safety.
Resistance groups in the hills are low on ammunition and medical supplies. A ground team will switch on a homing beacon for a short window tonight. Drop the canisters on the beacon.
A friendly unit is surrounded and cannot be reached by road. They will light a beacon at the drop zone. Deliver the supply pod there on time; they will not hold out much longer without it.
Our people on the ground need radios and batteries to keep reporting. Fly to the beacon and release the container while it transmits. Miss the window and they go another week without contact.
Partisans have planned a large raid and need explosives and night sights before they move. Their beacon will transmit only during the agreed window. Drop the load on it.
A downed aircrew is being sheltered by villagers who need food and medicine. A beacon marks the field they have chosen. Release the supplies there and keep low on the way in.
An observation team has run out of water and spares. Find their beacon in the dark and put the canister down within reach of it.
The enemy has moved a search radar into a new position. Its coverage overlaps the route our strike packages will use. Bring back pictures of the site so the planners can work around it.
Signals intelligence has picked up a radar we have not seen before. We need photographs of the antenna and the vehicles around it to identify the system.
An air defence radar has been dug in and camouflaged. Get close enough for clear pictures; analysts want to know which missile batteries it is feeding.
A search radar is giving the enemy early warning of every flight we launch. Take it off the air so the next waves can get through unseen.
This radar ties several missile sites into one network. Knock it out and the batteries around it go blind until it is replaced.
Destroy the radar before tomorrow's strikes. While it is working, nothing reaches the targets behind it without being tracked.
A mobile missile battery keeps changing position and has already shot down two of our aircraft. It has been located again. Destroy it before it moves on.
Self-propelled missile launchers are covering the approaches to the front. One unit has stopped for resupply. Hit it while it is standing still.
We finally have a fix on a roaming SAM unit. It will not stay long. Get there and destroy it.
A long-range radar installation can see our aircraft long before they reach the border. Photograph the site; we need its layout and the condition of the arrays.
The enemy is upgrading a strategic early-warning radar. Bring back pictures of the new antenna work so we can judge what it will be able to see.
Analysts suspect a long-range radar is being used to cue fighters far beyond its normal range. Photographs of the site will tell us how.
This early-warning radar gives the enemy hours of notice of any air attack. Destroying it opens a gap in their coverage that our bombers can use.
The long-range radar is the anchor of the enemy's warning chain. Put it out of action and their fighters will be scrambling blind.
Destroy the radar arrays. Without them the enemy cannot see deep into our territory, and our tankers can move closer.
Photograph the designated installation and return with the film.
Bring back clear pictures of the target site.
Reconnaissance of the target is needed before any further planning.
Destroy the designated installation.
The target must be put out of action.
Strike the target and return.
Fuel output from this refinery seems to have doubled in a month. Photograph the plant so we can see what has been built and where the product is going.
We need current pictures of the refinery. Reports say part of it has been converted for military fuels.
A refinery near the coast has gone onto a war footing. Photograph the units and the storage areas.
This refinery keeps the enemy's armoured units moving. Cut its output and their vehicles start running dry within days.
Hit the refinery's process units. Burning tanks are easy to repair; the columns and crackers are not.
The refinery supplies aviation fuel to every airbase in the region. Destroy it and their sortie rate will collapse.
A fuel depot has been expanded with new storage tanks. Photograph it so we can estimate how much fuel the enemy is stockpiling.
Bring back pictures of the fuel storage area. The number of full tanks tells us how soon an offensive can start.
A depot has been receiving tanker trucks around the clock. Photograph the tank farm and the loading area.
The enemy has built up a fuel reserve at this depot for the coming offensive. Set it on fire.
Destroy the storage tanks. Fuel stocks at the front are thin, and this depot is what keeps them topped up.
Columns are refuelling at this tank farm before moving forward. Take it out and they stall on the road.
A tank farm supplies the patrol boats and coastal units. Destroy it and they stay in harbour.
Fuel stored here keeps the enemy's helicopters flying. Burn it.
The depot holds fuel for the next month of operations. Hit the tanks and the loading pumps.
A new aircraft type has been seen on the ramp of this base. We need detailed photographs of it before it is moved into a shelter.
Satellites have caught a glimpse of an unfamiliar aircraft parked on the apron. Get close-up pictures; its wing and inlets will tell us what it can do.
A prototype is undergoing trials at this airbase. Photograph it on the ground. Every detail counts.
A prototype aircraft is about to finish its trials here. Destroy it on the ramp and set the programme back by years.
The aircraft parked at this base is the only flying example of a new design. Make sure it never flies again.
Destroy the aircraft on the apron before it is moved. It carries equipment we cannot allow the enemy to put into service.
A transport aircraft at this base is being fitted with unusual antennas. Photograph it so the analysts can work out what it is for.
An aircraft flown in under heavy escort is now parked at this base. Bring back pictures of it.
We think a command aircraft has been based here. Photographs of it will settle the question.
An airborne command post has been parked here between missions. Destroy it while it is on the ground.
The special aircraft at this base relays targeting data to the enemy's fighters. Take it out.
Destroy the aircraft on the ramp. Replacing it will take the enemy many months.
A cargo aircraft has landed with a shipment we cannot identify. Photograph it while the cargo is still on the ramp.
Something important has been flown in and is being unloaded now. We need pictures before it disappears into the hangars.
An aircraft carrying new weapons has arrived. Photograph the unloading before the crates are moved.
A transport is unloading missile components at this base. Destroy the aircraft before the cargo is taken away.
Weapons are being flown in for a new air defence site. Hit the aircraft and its cargo on the ramp.
A shipment of advanced electronics is coming off a transport aircraft. Destroy both before it is dispersed.
A training camp has grown fast in the last weeks. Photograph it so we can see how many fighters are being trained there.
Insurgent instructors are reported at this camp. Bring back pictures of the buildings and vehicles.
We need photographs of the camp before any decision is taken. Fly low enough for detail.
Fighters trained at this camp have carried out attacks across the region. Destroy it.
The camp is getting ready to send out another group. Hit it before they leave.
Leaders of an armed group are meeting at this camp. Destroy it while they are there.
The enemy carrier has put to sea with a new air group. Photograph the flight deck so we can count the aircraft.
The carrier has been refitted. Get pictures of the island and the deck; we want to see what has changed.
Bring back photographs of the carrier and its escorts. Its movements will decide where our fleet deploys.
The enemy carrier threatens our sea lanes. Damage it badly enough to send it back to the shipyard.
Strike the carrier while its escorts are spread out. Hits on the flight deck stop it launching aircraft.
The carrier is the heart of the enemy's surface group. Without it the fleet has no air cover.
Fast patrol craft have been harassing shipping. Photograph the boats and whatever they are carrying.
A new class of missile boat has been seen. Bring back pictures of its launchers.
Patrol boats have been operating from a new base. Photograph them in harbour.
A missile boat is preparing to sortie against our convoys. Destroy it before it leaves harbour.
Patrol craft are about to lay mines in the shipping channel. Sink them before they get under way.
Missile boats are waiting for the order to attack our ships. Destroy them first.
A missile boat is getting ready to strike our ships offshore. Sink it before it can fire.
Patrol boats are escorting a supply run along the coast. Destroy them before they reach port.
A fast attack craft has been shadowing our ships. Destroy it in time.
The enemy patrol boats keep watch over the coast. Sinking them opens the shore to our raiders.
Destroy the patrol craft. They warn coastal defences of every ship and aircraft that approaches.
These boats have been running weapons to insurgents. Destroy them.
A ballistic missile has been moved into a firing position. Photograph it so we can see how ready it is.
We need pictures of the missile site. Fuel trucks and crew vehicles around it would mean it is close to launch.
A missile launcher has been seen near the border. Bring back photographs of it.
A ballistic missile is being prepared for launch at our cities. Destroy it on the pad.
Missiles from this site can reach our rear bases. Destroy the launcher before it fires.
Intelligence says a launch is near. Take out the missile and its support vehicles.
A new missile site has been built along a busy air corridor. Photograph the launchers and the radar vans.
We need pictures of this SAM battery. Our planners want to know which missile it fires.
Bring back photographs of the missile site so we can plan a route around it.
This SAM battery has been covering the approaches to an important target. Destroy it to clear the way.
The missile site has shot at our aircraft before. Destroy its launchers.
Take out the SAM battery before tomorrow's strike passes over it.
An offshore platform is being used as an observation post. Photograph the equipment on the deck.
Bring back pictures of the oil platform. We think radar and guns have been mounted there.
An offshore rig may be refuelling patrol boats. Photograph it.
The offshore platform has been turned into a radar picket. Destroy it.
Gunners on this platform have fired on passing ships. Put it out of action.
Destroy the oil rig. Its output pays for the enemy's war.
A nuclear facility is suspected of producing weapons material. Photograph the site.
Bring back pictures of the reactor buildings. Inspectors were turned away last month.
We need photographs of the nuclear facility to confirm reports of new construction.
This facility is close to producing material for nuclear weapons. Destroy the reactor before it goes into operation.
Strike the nuclear facility. Once the reactor is running it can no longer be hit safely.
Destroy the reactor buildings. There may not be another chance.
The northern fleet's submarine pens are being reinforced. Photograph the new construction.
Bring back pictures of the submarine base. We need to know how many boats are in port.
A new submarine has arrived at the pens. Get photographs of it.
The submarine pens shelter the boats that threaten our convoys. Destroy them.
Strike the pens while the boats are in port for maintenance.
Destroy the submarine base. Every boat that stays in port is one fewer in the Atlantic.
A freighter is unloading cargo under armed guard. Photograph it before the crates are taken inland.
Bring back pictures of the ship in port. The cargo is believed to be weapons.
A cargo ship has arrived from abroad. Photograph the unloading.
A freighter is delivering weapons to the enemy. Sink it while the cargo is still on board.
Destroy the cargo ship before it is fully unloaded.
The ship carries missiles for the coastal batteries. Sink it at the quay.
A ballistic missile submarine is in port. Photograph it.
We need photographs of the submarine and its support vessels.
Bring back pictures of the missile submarine before it sails.
A missile submarine is getting ready to sail on patrol. Destroy it in harbour.
Strike the submarine before it reaches open water.
The submarine carries missiles aimed at our cities. Sink it.
Supplies are being stockpiled in the jungle along the trail. Photograph the dump.
Bring back pictures of the supply area. We need to know how much is coming down the trail.
A large supply dump has been reported under the tree cover. Photograph it.
The dump feeds the units fighting further south. Destroy it.
Strike the supply dump before the stocks are moved forward.
Destroy the supplies stored here. Trucks will take weeks to replace them.
A headquarters has moved into new buildings. Photograph the site.
Bring back pictures of the command post. The antennas will tell us who uses it.
We need photographs of the headquarters before the strike planners can work.
This headquarters directs the enemy's operations in the region. Destroy it.
Strike the command post. Without it the front units lose their coordination.
Senior officers use this headquarters. Hit it.
A command post coordinates the coastal defences. Destroy it.
Destroy the headquarters before the next offensive begins.
The headquarters is the communications hub of the enemy's forces. Take it out.
A planning conference is taking place at this headquarters. Hit it while it is in session.
Commanders are meeting here to plan an offensive. Destroy the headquarters before they leave.
Strike the headquarters now; the staff will have moved on by morning.
A bridge has been repaired. Photograph it to confirm it is open to traffic.
Bring back pictures of the bridge. We need to know whether it can carry tanks.
Photograph the bridge and the defences around it.
This bridge carries the main supply route to the front. Drop it.
Destroy the bridge before the armoured columns cross.
Cutting this bridge will force the enemy onto longer and more exposed roads.
A transport aircraft carrying senior officers will take off on a known route. Shoot it down.
We have the route of a transport carrying weapons experts. Intercept it.
A transport is ferrying spare parts to a fighter base. Intercept it on the way.
A transport aircraft is due on a known route with a shipment of missile parts. Shoot it down.
Intercept the transport. It carries technicians for the air defence network.
A cargo flight will fly a fixed route tonight. Make sure it does not land.
A reconnaissance aircraft has photographed our positions and is heading home. Shoot it down.
An intelligence-gathering aircraft is returning to base. Intercept it before it lands.
An aircraft on a spying flight is on its way back. Stop it.
An aircraft carrying a defector's family is flying back to the enemy. Shoot it down before it lands.
A courier aircraft with stolen documents is on its way home. Intercept it.
An aircraft is returning with film of our new airfield. Destroy it before it reaches base.
An unmarked aircraft has been delivering weapons and is now heading home. Intercept it.
A smuggling flight is returning to its base. Shoot it down.
An aircraft that carried arms to insurgents is on its way back. Intercept it.
A transport aircraft will leave with equipment we must not allow out of the country. Shoot it down after takeoff.
An aircraft with a high-value passenger is about to leave. Intercept it.
A transport is leaving with stolen technology. Shoot it down.
A long-range bomber is on patrol near our fleet. Shoot it down.
A maritime patrol aircraft is tracking our ships. Destroy it.
A bomber is flying a reconnaissance pattern. Shoot it down.
An airborne radar aircraft is directing fighters against us. Shoot it down.
The enemy's early-warning aircraft is on station. Destroy it.
Shoot down the radar aircraft. Without it, their fighters are blind.
Enemy fighters are on patrol over the area. Engage them.
A fighter patrol is guarding the approaches. Shoot them down.
Clear the sky of the enemy fighter patrol.
A palace is being used as a command bunker. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the palace compound. Communications equipment has been reported there.
We need photographs of the palace and its bunkers.
The palace has been turned into a command centre. Destroy it.
Strike the palace bunkers. The leadership has been using them.
Destroy the palace's command facilities.
A factory is suspected of producing chemical weapons. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the chemical plant. We need evidence.
We need photographs of the chemical weapons plant.
The chemical weapons plant must be destroyed before its stocks are used.
Strike the chemical plant and its storage bunkers.
Destroy the factory producing chemical agents.
A mobile missile launcher has been sighted. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the launcher and its support vehicles.
We need photographs of the mobile launcher's hiding place.
A mobile missile launcher is preparing to fire. Destroy it before it launches.
Destroy the launcher before it fires on our bases.
Strike the mobile launcher before it moves to a new firing point.
New hangars have been built at this airbase. Photograph them.
Bring back pictures of the hangars and the aircraft around them.
We need photographs of the hangar complex.
The hangars shelter the enemy's best fighters. Destroy them.
Strike the hangars before the aircraft inside are ready to fly.
Destroy the maintenance hangars at the base.
A laboratory is suspected of producing biological weapons. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the laboratory complex.
We need photographs of the biological weapons facility.
The biological weapons laboratory must be destroyed.
Destroy the laboratory before its products are used.
Strike the biological weapons facility.
A missile boat threatens the coalition fleet. Sink it.
Destroy the missile boat before it attacks our ships.
Sink the fast attack craft before it can fire.
The enemy plans to pump oil into the sea. Destroy the pumping manifold.
Destroy the pumping station before it floods the gulf with oil.
Strike the oil manifold and stop the spill.
A missile launcher is aimed at our cities. Destroy it.
Destroy the fixed missile launcher.
Strike the launcher before it fires again.
The air defence command centre has been located. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the air defence headquarters.
We need photographs of the command bunker.
The air defence command centre ties the enemy's SAMs and fighters together. Destroy it.
Strike the air defence headquarters and blind the network.
Destroy the command centre that runs the enemy's air defences.
A trawler is running weapons along the coast. Sink it.
Destroy the trawler before it lands its cargo.
The trawler is a spy ship. Sink it.
A trawler has been loitering near our naval base. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the trawler and its antennas.
We need photographs of the suspicious trawler.
Weapons for insurgents are stored at this dump. Destroy it.
Destroy the supply dump before its contents are shipped out.
Strike the supply dump.
A supply dump has been set up near the coast. Photograph it.
Bring back pictures of the supply dump.
We need photographs of the stored supplies.
Republican Guard units are dug in. Photograph their positions.
Bring back pictures of the Guard's armour.
We need photographs of the Guard division's positions.
Republican Guard armour is moving forward. Destroy it.
Strike the Guard units before they reach the front.
Destroy the Republican Guard positions.
roe: Nobody may learn we were there. Avoid every aircraft and ground unit you can. Do not fire unless your own aircraft is in danger, and do not leave anything behind that could be traced to us.
This flight does not officially exist. Stay unseen, keep clear of populated areas and only use your weapons on the objectives. If you are detected, break off and come home.
We are not at war. Get in and out without being seen. Weapons are for the assigned targets and for self-defence only.
Hostilities are limited. You may engage anything that threatens you or your objectives, but keep clear of civilian areas and do not cross into neutral airspace.
We are in a limited conflict. Enemy military targets may be engaged if they get in the way. Avoid civilian casualties at all costs.
The situation is tense but not open war. Defend yourself and hit the assigned targets; leave everything else alone.
We are at war. Every enemy military target is fair game.
Full hostilities. Engage the enemy wherever you find them, but stay clear of civilian targets.
Open war. Use your weapons as you see fit against enemy forces.

photo_at: Get reconnaissance photos of the {what} at {place}
suffix_unloading: by {deadline}, while its cargo is still there.
before {deadline}, while it is being unloaded.
no later than {deadline}, before the cargo is moved.
drop: Drop the supplies on the beacon at {coord}. It transmits until {deadline}.
Release the cargo over the beacon at {coord} before {deadline}.
Deliver the supply pod to the beacon at {coord} by {deadline}.
airstrip: Land at the strip at {coord} before {deadline} and take the cargo aboard.
Touch down at {coord} by {deadline} to pick up the cargo.
Make the pickup at the airstrip at {coord} before {deadline}.
route: A transport leaves {origin} at {depart} for {place}. Shoot it down before {deadline}.
Intercept the transport flying from {origin} to {place} (takeoff {depart}) by {deadline}.
The transport takes off from {origin} at {depart}, bound for {place}. Stop it before {deadline}.
leaving: A transport takes off from {place} at {depart}. Shoot it down.
last_seen: The aircraft was last seen at {coord} at {depart}, heading for {place}. Shoot it down before {deadline}.
Intercept the aircraft spotted at {coord} at {depart} on its way to {place}, by {deadline}.
Track down the aircraft seen at {coord} at {depart}, bound for {place}. Stop it before {deadline}.
